items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I eventually met Ward and saw him quite often

ctx.x: It was revenge in a satisfactory way because we had always been a better swing band then Alex Jackson's and we proved it these two nights. We threw everything except the kitchen stove at them and after every set we went off of our stand with the dancers still applauding and after every set it would be 10 minutes before Alex could start his set. In a certain way I felt sorry for them. They had been big shots in Ohio and perhaps other places, but they received a lesson in how jazz should be played for two nights…

I had been told about a trumpet player named Ward Pinkett who was said to be one of the best in New York. I eventually met Ward and saw him quite often but never heard him play which I regretted very much. Ward was not in very good health and had been told by a doctor that he had only a few months to live. I think he was born in Virginia and he went home with the thought that maybe some rest would prolong his life, but he soon became lonesome for the gay life in New York and came back. He said that if he didn't…

The Lafayette Theatre located next door to Connie's Inn was the most popular gathering place for Harlem entertainers in New York and the Rhythm Club was just around the corner from the Lafayette. So there was always plenty of activities in that block between 131st and 132 street with all the musicians going/in and out of the club and the show people all along the block in front of the Lafayette and Connie's.
